# swarm_cluster (Resource)

A Docker Swarm cluster and its nodes. Each create and update reconciles the cluster from what Docker says: it adopts the cluster its managers are in, or the first manager by name inits one; the nodes in no swarm join it, managers first; promotions come before demotions; and the nodes the configuration no longer has are drained until their tasks run elsewhere, demoted, made to leave, and removed. A change that would keep fewer than a majority of the managers ready is refused at plan time: add the new managers in one apply, remove the old ones in the next. Destroying it keeps the cluster, unless `leave_on_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "swarm_cluster" "this" {
  nodes = {
    "node-1" = {
      endpoint       = "tcp://10.0.0.11:2376"
      advertise_addr = "10.0.0.11"
      role           = "manager"
      labels         = { zone = "a" }
    }
    "node-2" = {
      endpoint       = "tcp://10.0.0.12:2376"
      advertise_addr = "10.0.0.12"
      role           = "manager"
      labels         = { zone = "b" }
    }
    "node-3" = {
      endpoint       = "tcp://10.0.0.13:2376"
      advertise_addr = "10.0.0.13"
      role           = "manager"
      labels         = { zone = "c" }
    }
    "node-4" = {
      endpoint     = "ssh://deploy@10.0.0.14"
      role         = "worker"
      availability = "drain"
    }
  }

  tls = {
    ca_pem   = file("ca.pem")
    cert_pem = file("cert.pem")
    key_pem  = file("key.pem")
  }

  init = {
    default_addr_pool = ["10.20.0.0/16"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `nodes` (Attributes Map) The nodes, by a name of the configuration's choosing, which is not Docker's hostname. At least one is a `manager`. A node is matched to Docker's by the ID its daemon gives, so a changed endpoint that answers with the same ID is the same node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))

### Optional

- `init` (Attributes) The settings of `docker swarm init`, used when the cluster is created. Docker cannot change them afterwards: a change is refused. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--init))
- `leave_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroying the resource makes every node leave the swarm. Default: `false`, the cluster stays and Terraform forgets it.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `tls` (Attributes) The TLS of the nodes' `tcp://` endpoints, for those that give none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tls))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The cluster's ID, as Docker gives it.
- `join_tokens` (Attributes) The tokens to join the cluster with. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--join_tokens))
- `manager_addresses` (List of String) The managers' addresses, `HOST:PORT`, that nodes join.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Required:

- `endpoint` (String) The node's Docker: `tcp://HOST:PORT`, in TLS when `tls` is given, `ssh://USER@HOST` or `unix:///PATH`. It may be unknown at plan time, when the machine is created in the same apply: the provider waits until it answers.

Optional:

- `advertise_addr` (String) The address the other nodes reach this one on. Default: Docker's choice.
- `availability` (String) `active`, `pause` or `drain`.
- `labels` (Map of String) The node's labels. Authoritative: a label the configuration does not give is removed.
- `role` (String) `manager` or `worker`.
- `tls` (Attributes) This node's TLS, instead of the cluster's `tls`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes--tls))

Read-Only:

- `node_id` (String) The node's ID in the cluster.
- `reachable` (Boolean) Whether the node's Docker answered when the cluster was last read.
- `status` (String) The node's state as the managers see it: `ready`, `down`, `disconnected` or `unknown`; `absent` when it is in no swarm.

<a id="nestedatt--nodes--tls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes.tls`

Optional:

- `ca_pem` (String) The CA of the daemon's certificate, in PEM. Default: the system's.
- `cert_pem` (String) The client's certificate, in PEM.
- `key_pem` (String, Sensitive) The client's key, in PEM.



<a id="nestedatt--init"></a>
### Nested Schema for `init`

Optional:

- `data_path_port` (Number) The UDP port of the overlay networks' traffic. Default: Docker's, 4789.
- `default_addr_pool` (List of String) The pools of the overlay networks' subnets, in CIDR. Default: Docker's, `10.0.0.0/8`.
- `subnet_size` (Number) The prefix length of each overlay network's subnet. Default: Docker's, 24.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--tls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tls`

Optional:

- `ca_pem` (String) The CA of the daemon's certificate, in PEM. Default: the system's.
- `cert_pem` (String) The client's certificate, in PEM.
- `key_pem` (String, Sensitive) The client's key, in PEM.


<a id="nestedatt--join_tokens"></a>
### Nested Schema for `join_tokens`

Read-Only:

- `manager` (String, Sensitive) A manager's.
- `worker` (String, Sensitive) A worker's.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = swarm_cluster.this
  id = "z7c2akjkcp231l8f6w91lta26"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The cluster's ID, as `docker info --format '{{.Swarm.Cluster.ID}}'` gives it on a manager.
terraform import swarm_cluster.this z7c2akjkcp231l8f6w91lta26
```
